title: Land to cultivate, yet no meal
literal_meaning: A bati of cultivation, yet fasting every day.
explanation: The joke places a substantial-looking agricultural resource beside an empty stomach. The source explains it as plenty of rice but too little cooked food. Possession and actual provision have come apart: what looks sufficient has not become something usable. The saying does not identify one universal cause for that mismatch.
meaning_odia: ଚାଷ ଅଛି, ଚାଉଳର ଅଭାବ ବି ନାହିଁ, ଅଥଚ ଖାଇବାକୁ ଭାତ ନିଅଣ୍ଟ। ଢଗଟିର ପରିହାସ ଏହି ବିରୋଧରେ। କାଗଜରେ ବା ଦେଖିବାକୁ ଯାହା ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ, ତାହା ଦରକାର ବେଳେ କାମରେ ଆସୁନାହିଁ। ଅଭାବର କାରଣଟି କଣ, ଏହି ଛୋଟ ଧାଡ଼ି ନିଜେ କହେନାହିଁ।
usage_example: A community room has cupboards full of donated supplies, but nobody can find the materials needed for today’s class. Someone recalls this mismatch between plenty and use. (Original imagined example.)
cultural_context: Bati is retained as the source’s land-measure term; no regional conversion is supplied. The witness spells the daily expression ନୀତି, which is preserved. The accompanying gloss, not an invented household story, supports the reading.
odia_summary: ସମ୍ବଳ ଥାଇ ବି ଦରକାର ବେଳେ ତାହାର ଫଳ ନମିଳିବାର ପରିହାସ।
english_summary: Abundant resources have not become a usable meal.
